$comentario_api: The backend's «no». It arrives as a code plus data —the backend does not write text for people (RN-30)— and the sentence is built here. One code per key, with the same name: api_<code>. Adding a code in the backend (app/utils/api_errors.py) without its key here makes `npm run check` fail.

$comentario_soporte: The support panel's «no»s and the subscription check (F3). Two carry a variant because the data they bring is the only thing that makes the sentence useful: «a limit was reached» does not say which resource filled up, and «you cannot operate» does not say what to pay.

$comentario_producto: When the backend sends the product id but not its name —because the row is gone— the sentence says «#47» instead of leaving a hole. And if it sends neither, «(unidentified)». The parentheses are not decoration: this text goes where a product name goes, and «the product unidentified» reads as broken English while «the product (unidentified)» reads as a name that is missing. Spanish gets away with «sin identificar» because the adjective follows the noun.
